0.comment: Capitano: Thrain, Sentinel Knight of Khaenri'ah
0.content: Before he was Capitano, Thrain was a high-ranking knight and Commander of Khaenri'ah under the Eclipse Dynasty, honored as a Sentinel Knight. He watched the Abyss destroy his nation, family and comrades, a pain he says five hundred years has not dulled. He resisted, judged the situation unsalvageable, and fled with what remained of his platoon. As a Khaenri'ahn survivor he bears Ronova's curse of immortality, and he blames her for punishing a whole people when most knew nothing of the Five Sinners' crimes, himself included.

1.content: His heart was modified with Khaenri'ahn technology to convert memories and souls drawn from the Ley Lines into knowledge. After encountering countless lost souls in the disasters, he gave up that function and made it a vessel. The souls of his fallen comrades (Guthred among them) and of Natlanese who could not enter the Ley Lines lived inside him for five centuries. Ororon, sensitive to souls, heard a voice from his heart and sensed something like a soul trying to escape; the Lord of the Night suggests the endless voices are why Ororon never saw him sleep. His hidden purpose in Natlan was always to use his death to open the gates of the Ley Lines for them.

2.content: Fleeing Khaenri'ah, Thrain's platoon reached Natlan and found it suffering the same Abyssal tragedy. Many blamed Khaenri'ahns, but Ayizu, chief of the Masters of the Night-Wind, treated him with kindness and helped him. From then on he made Natlan's survival his mission. Ayizu told him the secret of the Pyro Gnosis in his last moments, and Thrain came to resent Mavuika for prolonging the inevitable. Natlan remembers him as a legendary hero who fought beside the Night-Wind.

3.content: Capitano came to Natlan to seize the Pyro Gnosis, convinced Mavuika's war against the Abyss was hopeless. In A Decision (5.0) he stormed the Stadium of the Sacred Flame with the Fatui; their duel ended when a single full-power strike from her wounded him, and smoke from the Masters of the Night-Wind (Ororon's spell) carried him away. Later he refused his subordinate Rezanov's suggestion to take the weakened Archon's Gnosis: "I have never taken advantage of an opponent in a time of weakness." He also told the Traveler that, having been defeated, he must put his thoughts of the Gnosis to rest. She told him it felt like fighting the pinnacle of human strength.

4.comment: Capitano: Ororon and the Source Mechanism
4.content: In Natlan, Capitano hunted for Citlali, the legendary Granny Itztli believed able to speak to the Wayob and so to the Night Kingdom. He approached Ororon of her tribe, saw through his lies and let him trail him. Ororon saved his life in the duel, then in a secret cave pressed him, citing that debt and his sense of justice, until Capitano revealed his plan of rebuilding the Ley Lines. His men gathered the scholars' research to locate an ancient Source Mechanism.

5.comment: Capitano: Guthred and the Draught of Lucidity
5.content: Guthred was Capitano's former second-in-command and a respected military doctor. They differed on justice, and Guthred felt Capitano lost chances to win whenever he indulged his honor, yet Capitano treated their differences as what made them good partners. To cure soldiers deluded by the Abyss into killing one another, Guthred developed the Draught of Lucidity, using himself as the test subject, and died soon after. The draught dispels the Abyss's psychological damage but leaves lifelong migraines.

6.comment: Capitano: Sacrifice and merging with the Lord of the Night
6.content: In When All Becomes a Monument (5.3), Ronova came to collect Mavuika's death. The Lord of the Night hesitated and announced that another would take her place; Capitano arrived and thanked Ororon for showing him the way. If he died for Mavuika, Ronova would get her death, but his curse of immortality would negate it, creating a paradox that could uproot the natural order. He told her to forsake one of her rules; Ronova upheld the curse. He merged with the Lord of the Night, so she can never die and her eternal life can mend Natlan's Ley Lines. His body remains dormant on the Throne of the Primal Fire.

7.content: Capitano commanded the Fatui armed forces and was therefore a Councillor in the Snezhnograd Veche. Before leaving for Natlan he wrote Pierro a detailed letter that was effectively his will, reassigning his key subordinates, most of his troops and his Veche seat to Tartaglia. Pierro revealed it only after Natlan was resolved. Marionette explains that Capitano knew Pulcinella and Pantalone would otherwise take his army, and the letter gave Pierro a reason to back Tartaglia.

8.comment: Capitano: Vesna and Danica, his pupils
8.content: Capitano trained Vesna Strivozha, the Vila heiress who carries a fragment of Life's authority, and Danica. Vesna expected Pulcinella as her mentor, but at her audience she was given a Druzhna recruit's badge and the First Harbinger as her teacher ("This was Capitano's idea," Pulcinella announced). At the training grounds he told her she had no reason to doubt herself and insisted: "You should call me Teacher." When she feared losing a power that was never truly hers, he took off his mask and showed that he carried a power of the same order, adding that even stripped of it he would be no lesser a man. He later told her not to rely too heavily on power that isn't her own unless she truly has nowhere left to turn.

9.content: At Signora's funeral Capitano said that though her methods tarnished her honor, her loss was a great pity, then pressed Dottore about Scaramouche and the Electro Gnosis. Rank-and-file Fatui call him "the ever-righteous Captain" and "the nigh-invincible Captain"; Viktor, a Fatui running an errand for Signora in Mondstadt, says that if he could choose he would prefer to work under him.

10.comment: Capitano: Varka and the Nod-Krai expedition
10.content: During Varka's Knights of Favonius expedition, the Knights' vanguard clashed with Fatui scouts and both sides called for reinforcements until Capitano and his elite subordinates faced Varka's battle line at night. Capitano and Varka spoke briefly and agreed to part peacefully; Varka said he would have loved to duel him if not for their circumstances, and that Capitano knew a battle in a foreign land would hurt them both (Mika's character story). Varka's character teaser shows Capitano giving him intelligence on the Abyssal calamity. In Nod-Krai, Leifhelm ranks Capitano as the only person met on the expedition whose strength compares to Varka's.

11.content: In the limited-time event story Those We Have Lost, Capitano asked Columbina where he might find Arlecchino for work matters and was sent to Sandrone's tea party, with Tartaglia following. When Sandrone challenged the uninvited guests, he apologised, explained, and promised not to sully the gathering with work until afterward.
